ser-identity.x: Use "ser" to say who someone is, where they are from, and their job. Examples: "soy", "es".

estar-location.x: Use "estar" to say where a person, place or thing is. Examples: "está", "están".

estar-feelings.x: Use "estar" for how someone feels or a temporary state. Examples: "estoy cansado", "está contenta".

ser-estar-intro.x: Use "ser" for lasting traits like origin, job and identity. Use "estar" for temporary states and places. Examples: "es mexicano", "está enferma".

hay-existence.x: Use "hay" to say that something exists in a place. It stays the same for one or many things. Example: "Hay un parque."

present-ar.x: Regular -ar verbs take these endings: -o, -as, -a, -amos, -an. Examples: "hablo", "trabaja".

present-er-ir.x: Regular -er and -ir verbs take -o, -es, -e, -en. In the "nosotros" form they take -emos or -imos. Examples: "como", "escribe".

present-irregular-yo.t: Verbs with an irregular yo form
present-irregular-yo.x: Some verbs change only in the "yo" form. Hacer becomes "hago", salir becomes "salgo", poner becomes "pongo". The other forms are regular.

tener-present.x: Use "tener" to say how old you are and what you have. Forms: tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tienen. Example: "Tengo veinte años."

ir-present.x: Use "ir" with "a" to say where you go. Forms: voy, vas, va, vamos, van. Example: "Voy a la escuela."

stem-change-e-ie.x: In some verbs, the stem vowel e changes to ie in all forms except "nosotros". Examples: "quiero", "empieza", but "queremos".

stem-change-o-ue.x: In some verbs, the stem vowel o changes to ue in all forms except "nosotros". Examples: "puedo", "duerme", but "podemos".

reflexive-daily.x: Reflexive verbs use a pronoun before the verb: me, te, se, nos. The pronoun matches the subject. Example: "Yo me levanto."

gustar-basic.x: Use "gusta" for one thing or an action, and "gustan" for many things. The person who likes comes first: me, te, le, nos, les. Example: "Me gustan los gatos."

noun-gender.x: Every Spanish noun is masculine or feminine. Many nouns ending in -o are masculine and many ending in -a are feminine. Articles and adjectives must match. Example: "el libro rojo".

noun-plural.x: Add -s to nouns ending in a vowel and -es to nouns ending in a consonant. A final z changes to c before -es. Examples: "libros", "lápices".

definite-articles.x: Use el and la for one masculine or feminine noun, and los and las for many. They match the noun. Examples: "el niño", "las casas".

indefinite-articles.x: Use un and una for one new thing, and unos and unas for some. They match the noun. Examples: "un jardín", "unas flores".

adjective-agreement.x: Adjectives match the noun in gender and number. Change -o to -a for feminine and add -s for plural. Examples: "casa pequeña", "carros rápidos".

possessive-short.x: The short possessives are mi, tu, su, nuestro. They agree with the thing owned, not the owner. Add -s for plural. Examples: "mi casa", "mis libros".

demonstratives.x: Este means this, close to me. Ese means that, close to you. Aquel means that, far from both. They match the noun. Examples: "esta casa", "aquel parque".

subject-pronouns.x: The subject pronouns are yo, tú, él, ella, usted, nosotros, ustedes, ellos. Use them to make the subject clear or to contrast people. Example: "Yo trabajo y ella estudia."

question-words.x: Question words have an accent and start the question. Qué is what, quién is who, dónde is where, cuándo is when, cómo is how, cuántos is how many. Example: "¿Dónde vives?"

yes-no-questions.x: To ask a yes or no question, keep the word order and raise your voice. In writing, use ¿ and ?. Answer with "sí" or "no". Example: "¿Hablas inglés?"

negation-no.x: Put "no" before the verb to make a sentence negative. Do not add a word like "do". Examples: "No tengo hermanos.", "No me gusta el café."

prep-a-de-en.x: Use "a" for direction, "de" for origin or possession, and "en" for place. Examples: "Voy a Lima.", "Soy de Chile.", "Vivo en Quito."

contractions-al-del.x: Spanish joins "a" and "el" into "al", and "de" and "el" into "del". This happens only with "el". Examples: "al banco", "del trabajo".

numbers-0-100.x: Learn the numbers from cero to cien. From 31 to 99, join tens and ones with "y". Examples: "treinta y cinco", "noventa y ocho".

time-clock.x: Use "es la" for one o'clock and "son las" for other hours. Add "y media" for half past. Examples: "Es la una.", "Son las tres y media."

days-months-dates.x: The days are lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado, domingo. Say a date with a number and "de" before the month. Example: "el cinco de mayo".

weather-hacer.x: Use "hace" for most weather, like "hace calor" and "hace frío". Use "hay" with some nouns, like "hay lluvia". Use "llueve" for rain.

muy-mucho.x: Use "muy" before an adjective or adverb. Use "mucho" after a verb. Examples: "muy rico", "como mucho".

tambien-tampoco.x: Use "también" to agree with a positive sentence. Use "tampoco" to agree with a negative sentence. Examples: "Yo también trabajo.", "Ella tampoco come carne."

formal-usted.x: Use "tú" with friends, family and children. Use "usted" for polite speech with older or unknown people. Usted takes the same verb form as él and ella. Example: "¿Cómo está usted?"

basic-connectors.x: Use "y" to add, "pero" for contrast, "o" for a choice, and "porque" for a reason. Example: "Estudio español porque me gusta."

ir-a-near-future.x: Use a form of "ir", then "a", then an infinitive to say what you are going to do. Example: "Voy a comer."

pret-regular.x: Use the preterite for finished actions. For -ar verbs add -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -aron. For -er and -ir verbs add -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -ieron, as in "hablé" and "comí".

pret-ser-ir.t: Past tense of ser and ir
pret-ser-ir.x: The verbs "ser" and "ir" have the same preterite forms: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fueron. The context shows whether the meaning is "was" or "went".

pret-irregular-common.x: Some common verbs have an irregular stem in the preterite, such as "hacer" (hic-), "tener" (tuv-) and "dar" (di-). Their endings have no written accent, as in "hice" and "tuvo".

pret-stem-change-3rd.t: Past stem changes e to i
pret-stem-change-3rd.x: In the preterite, -ir verbs with a stem change in the present change e to i or o to u only in the third person: "pidió", "durmió", "pidieron", "durmieron".

pret-spelling-changes.x: In the preterite, some verbs change spelling to keep the sound. In the yo form, -car becomes -qué, -gar becomes -gué and -zar becomes -cé, as in "busqué" and "llegué".

imperfect-regular.x: Use the imperfect to describe habits and ongoing situations in the past. Add -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -aban to -ar verbs and -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían to -er and -ir verbs.

imperfect-irregular.x: Only three verbs are irregular in the imperfect: "ser" (era, eras, era, éramos, eran), "ir" (iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, iban) and "ver" (veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veían).

pret-vs-imperfect-intro.x: Use the imperfect for a background action in progress or a habit. Use the preterite for a finished action or a sudden event, as in "Dormía cuando sonó el teléfono."

present-progressive.x: To say what is happening now, use "estar" plus a gerund. The gerund ends in -ando for -ar verbs and -iendo for -er and -ir verbs, as in "estoy cocinando".

present-perfect-intro.x: To talk about recent experiences, use "haber" in the present plus a past participle: he, has, ha, hemos, han + hablado or comido. Example: "he comido".

participle-irregular.x: Some verbs have an irregular past participle, for example "hacer" gives "hecho", "ver" gives "visto", "abrir" gives "abierto" and "escribir" gives "escrito".

imperative-tu-affirmative.x: To give an affirmative command to someone you call "tú", use the third person present form: "abre", "cierra". Eight verbs are irregular, such as "ven", "di", "haz", "ve".

imperative-tu-negative.x: For a negative command with "tú", use "no" plus the present subjunctive form: "no abras", "no hables". The -ar verbs take -es and the -er and -ir verbs take -as.

imperative-usted.x: To give a polite command to someone you call "usted", use the present subjunctive form: "pase", "escriba". Add the reflexive pronoun after an affirmative command: "siéntese".

reflexive-more-verbs.x: Reflexive verbs keep their pronoun in every tense. Put me, te, se, nos or se before the conjugated verb, as in "me desperté" and "nos vestimos".

reciprocal-nos.x: To say that people do something to each other, use the plural pronouns "nos" or "se" with the verb, as in "nos vemos" and "se escriben".

gustar-type-verbs.x: With "gustar", "encantar" and "interesar", the verb agrees with the thing liked, not the person. Use "le gusta" for one thing and "le gustan" for several things.

indirect-object-pronouns.x: Indirect object pronouns tell who receives something: me, te, le, nos, les. They go before the conjugated verb, as in "Le doy un regalo".

direct-object-pronouns.x: Direct object pronouns replace the thing or person receiving the action: lo, la, los, las. They agree in gender and number with that noun and go before the verb.

pronoun-position-infinitive.x: With an infinitive or a gerund, the object pronoun can be attached to the end of the verb. Add an accent on the gerund, as in "verla" and "leyéndola".

prepositional-pronouns.x: After most prepositions, use these pronouns: mí, ti, él, ella, usted, nosotros, ellos. With "con", "mí" and "ti" become "conmigo" and "contigo".

personal-a.x: Put "a" before a direct object that is a specific person or a pet. Do not use it for things, as in "Veo a mi tío" but "Veo la casa".

saber-conocer.x: Use "saber" for facts and skills: "sé nadar". Use "conocer" for people and places you are familiar with: "conozco a Ana".

ser-estar-contrast.x: Use "ser" for lasting traits, such as "es alta". Use "estar" for a state or condition that can change, such as "está enfermo".

tener-que-hay-que.x: Use "tener que" plus an infinitive for a personal obligation: "tengo que". Use "hay que" plus an infinitive for a general rule, with no subject.

poder-querer-infinitive.x: After "poder" and "querer", use the infinitive directly with no preposition: "puedo ayudar", "quiero comer". Both verbs change the stem e to ie or o to ue.

acabar-de.x: Use "acabar de" plus an infinitive to say that something happened a moment ago. Conjugate only "acabar" in the present: "acabo de llegar".

por-para-basics.x: Use "para" for a purpose, a goal or a deadline, as in "para el viernes". Use "por" for a place you pass through or a reason, as in "por el parque" and "gracias por".

comparatives-regular.x: To compare two things, use "más" or "menos" plus an adjective, then "que": "Mi casa es más grande que la tuya".

superlatives.x: For the superlative, use the article plus "más" or "menos" and an adjective, then "de": "el más alto de la clase". The irregular forms are "mejor" and "peor".

tan-como.t: As much as, as many as
tan-como.x: To say two things are equal, use "tan" plus an adjective plus "como". With nouns, use "tanto" and match it to the noun: "tantos libros como tú".

adverbs-mente.x: To make many adverbs, add "-mente" to the feminine form of an adjective: "rápida" becomes "rápidamente". Keep the accent of the adjective, as in "fácilmente".

frequency-adverbs.x: Frequency adverbs say how often you do something: "siempre" always, "a veces" sometimes, "nunca" never. With "nunca" before the verb, do not add "no".

ya-todavia.x: Use "ya" to say that something has already happened. Use "todavía" to say that something is still true or has not happened yet, as in "todavía no".

numbers-100-plus.x: Hundreds agree with the noun in gender: "doscientos pesos", "doscientas casas". Use "cien" alone and "ciento" before other numbers, as in "ciento veinte".

ordinal-numbers.x: Ordinal numbers such as "primero", "segundo" and "tercero" agree with the noun. "Primero" and "tercero" become "primer" and "tercer" before a masculine noun.

place-prepositions.x: Phrases such as "debajo de", "enfrente de" and "cerca de" say where something is. Before "el", "de" becomes "del": "enfrente del banco".

time-hace.x: Use "hace" plus a time period after a past verb to say how long ago it happened: "Llegué hace una semana". Use "desde hace" for something that continues now.

question-por-que.x: Write "por qué" as two words with an accent for questions. Write "porque" as one word without an accent for answers: "¿Por qué estudias? Porque me gusta".

cause-consequence-simple.x: Use "porque" to give a reason. Use "así que" or "por eso" to give the result: "Llovía, así que me quedé en casa".

relative-que-simple.x: Use "que" to join a noun with more information about it. It can refer to people or things: "el libro que compré".

future-simple-regular.x: To talk about the future, add endings to the whole infinitive: -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án. Example: "hablaré", "comerán".

future-irregular.x: Some verbs change the stem in the future but keep the same endings: "tendr-", "har-", "podr-", "dir-", "saldr-", "vendr-".

future-probability.x: We can use the future tense to guess about the present. It means "probably". Example: "Estará en casa" means "He is probably at home".

conditional-polite.x: The conditional makes requests softer and more polite. Use "podría", "querría" and "me gustaría". Example: "¿Podría ayudarme?"

conditional-advice.x: To give advice, use the conditional of "deber" or the phrase "yo que tú" plus the conditional. Example: "Deberías descansar".

past-perfect.x: Use "había" plus a participle for a past action that happened before another past action. Example: "Ya había salido" means "He had already left".

pret-vs-imperfect-narrative.x: In a story, use the imperfect for the background and for repeated actions. Use the preterite for events that happen and finish. Example: "Dormía cuando sonó el teléfono".

pret-meaning-change.x: Some verbs change meaning in the preterite. "Supe" means "I found out", "conocí" means "I met", and "pude" means "I managed to".

perfect-vs-preterite.x: Use the present perfect for experience up to now or a period that is not finished. Use the preterite for a finished time. Example: "Esta semana he trabajado" and "Ayer trabajé".

past-progressive.x: Use "estaba" plus a gerund to describe an action in progress in the past. Example: "Estaba cocinando cuando llegaste".

subj-present-forms.x: For the present subjunctive, take the "yo" form of the present, remove -o, and add the opposite vowel: -e for -ar verbs, -a for -er and -ir verbs. Example: "tenga", "cierres".

subj-wishes.x: After verbs of wanting, asking and preferring, use "que" and the subjunctive when the subject changes. Example: "Quiero que vengas".

subj-emotion.x: After expressions of feeling, such as "me alegra que" and "lamento que", use the subjunctive when the subject changes. Example: "Me alegra que estés aquí".

subj-doubt.x: After doubt or denial, such as "dudo que" and "no creo que", use the subjunctive. Example: "Dudo que llegue".

subj-impersonal.x: After phrases such as "es importante que", "es mejor que" and "es posible que", use the subjunctive. Example: "Es mejor que vayas".

subj-recommend.x: After verbs such as "recomendar", "pedir" and "sugerir", use "que" and the subjunctive. Example: "Te recomiendo que leas este libro".

subj-irregular-forms.x: Six common verbs have irregular present subjunctive forms: "sea" (ser), "esté" (estar), "vaya" (ir), "sepa" (saber), "haya" (haber) and "dé" (dar).

subj-cuando-future.x: When "cuando" refers to a future event that has not happened yet, use the subjunctive. Example: "Cuando llegue, te llamo".

subj-para-que.x: Use "para que" and the subjunctive to say the purpose of an action when the other clause has a different subject. Example: "Te lo explico para que lo entiendas".

indicative-vs-subjunctive.x: After "creo que" and "pienso que", use the indicative. After "no creo que", use the subjunctive. Example: "Creo que viene" and "No creo que venga".

imperative-clitics-affirmative.x: In affirmative commands, attach the pronouns to the end of the verb. Often a written accent is needed. Example: "Dímelo" and "Siéntate".

imperative-clitics-negative.x: In negative commands, put the pronouns before the verb, and use the subjunctive form. Example: "No me lo digas".

imperative-ustedes.x: To give a command to a group, use the "ustedes" form of the present subjunctive. Example: "Pasen" and "Siéntense".

double-object-pronouns.x: When two object pronouns appear together, the indirect one goes first: "me lo", "te la", "nos los". Example: "Me lo dio".

se-lo-rule.t: Se before lo, la, los, las
se-lo-rule.x: When "le" or "les" comes before "lo", "la", "los" or "las", it changes to "se". Example: "Se lo expliqué" and not "le lo expliqué".

se-accidental.x: Use "se" plus "me", "te", "le", "nos" or "les" for something that happens by accident. The verb agrees with the thing, not the person. Example: "Se me cayó el vaso".

passive-se.x: Use "se" and the verb to say what is done without saying who does it. The verb agrees with the thing. Example: "Se vende casa" and "Se venden casas".

impersonal-se.x: Use "se" with a singular verb to talk about people in general, without a specific subject. Example: "Se puede entrar".

passive-ser-intro.x: To say what was done to something, use "ser" plus a participle. The participle agrees with the noun. Example: "La casa fue construida".

llevar-gerund.x: Use "llevar" plus a time expression and a gerund to say how long you have been doing something. Example: "Llevo un año estudiando".

seguir-gerund.x: Use "seguir" plus a gerund to say that an action continues. Example: "Sigo trabajando" means "I am still working".

soler-volver-a.x: Use "soler" plus an infinitive for what you usually do. Use "volver a" plus an infinitive for doing something again. Example: "Suelo caminar" and "Vuelvo a llamar".

deber-deber-de.x: Use "deber" plus an infinitive for obligation. Use "deber de" plus an infinitive for a guess. Example: "Debes dormir" and "Debe de estar cansado".

comparatives-irregular.x: Four comparatives are irregular: "mejor" (better), "peor" (worse), "mayor" (older) and "menor" (younger). Do not use "más" before them.

adjective-position.x: Before a masculine singular noun, "bueno" and "malo" become "buen" and "mal". Before any singular noun, "grande" becomes "gran" and means "great". Example: "un buen amigo", "una gran ciudad".

relative-quien-donde.x: Use "quien" for a person, "donde" for a place, and "lo que" for an idea or thing in general. Example: "La mujer con quien hablé".

lo-neutral.x: Use "lo" plus a masculine singular adjective to talk about an idea in general. Example: "Lo importante" means "the important thing".

si-real-conditions.x: For a likely condition, use "si" plus the present. The result is in the present or the future. Example: "Si llueve, nos quedamos".

si-hypothetical.x: For an unlikely or imaginary situation, use "si" plus the imperfect subjunctive, and the conditional in the result. Example: "Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría".

por-para-contrast.x: Use "por" for cause, thanks and exchange. Use "para" for the person who receives something and for a deadline. Example: "Es para ti" and "Gracias por todo".

verb-preposition-pairs.x: Some verbs always take a certain preposition: "soñar con", "pensar en", "depender de". Learn the verb and its preposition together.

aunque-indicative.x: Use "aunque" with the indicative when you state a fact that you know is true. Example: "Aunque estoy cansado, sigo trabajando".

reported-simple.x: To report what someone said, use "dijo que" and move the verb into the past. Example: "Ana dijo: Estoy cansada" becomes "Ana dijo que estaba cansada".

indirect-questions.x: After phrases such as "no sé", "me preguntó" and "dime", the question word keeps its accent but there are no question marks. Example: "No sé dónde vive".

tag-questions.x: Add "¿verdad?" or "¿no?" at the end of a statement to ask the listener to confirm it. Example: "Vienes mañana, ¿verdad?"

exclamations-que.x: Use "qué" before an adjective in an exclamation. Use "cuánto" or "cuánta" before a noun, and match the noun. Example: "¡Qué bonito!" and "¡Cuánta gente!"

diminutives.x: Add -ito or -ita to a word to say small or to show affection. The ending matches the gender and number of the noun. Example: "perrito", "casita".

years-dates-long.x: Say years in full: "mil novecientos noventa" or "dos mil veinticinco". Say dates as day, "de", month, "de", year. Example: "el cinco de marzo de dos mil veinticinco".
